# Create Samebase repository (`create_repository`)

MCP tool `repository_create` · scope `access_app_create` · write

Creates a GitHub repository under the selected organization's verified GitHub owner, seeds the
starter template, records the Samebase repository, and starts managed setup of its first app. Setup
always creates a Convex project with one production deployment. It uses convexDeploymentRegion when
supplied. Otherwise, it uses the organization default, which is US East when no default is saved.

Samebase picks the Workers Builds token: the given buildTokenUuid, else the available last-used
token, else the only token. Several tokens and no last-used one return an error that lists their
names and UUIDs. With a token, setup also creates a Cloudflare Worker and configures Workers Builds
for the repository (pushes to the default branch deploy, and pull requests get preview deploys) with
Convex deploy keys in production and Previews Base Builds settings. The result reports
cloudflare.state planned with the Worker name.

When the Cloudflare account has no token, setup creates no Worker and stops after GitHub and Convex
are ready. The result reports cloudflare.state pending with the setup guide,
https://samebase.com/docs/cloudflare-setup: use Cloudflare's standard repository setup to create the
first account token, delete the temporary Worker, then call repository_cloudflare_createWorker for
this repository.

Preconditions: the caller must be an organization member. Its GitHub App installation and selected
Convex and Cloudflare provider connections must be available. The GitHub repository and Convex
project names must be available, and the Worker name when a token is used. A name collision fails
the call before any repository or run is created, so pick a different name and call again; failures
after setup starts surface through `repository_list` instead.

What it writes: one repository (private by default) and one Convex project with one production
deployment in the resolved region. With a token, it also writes one Worker with native Worker
Previews. Production Builds and Previews Base Builds each carry `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` with the
matching Convex key. All resources live in the organization's provider accounts. Deleting the
Samebase account does not remove or stop any of them.

Progress and failure are readable through `repository_list`: `providerSetup.status` is running,
ready, or failed; on failure it names the provider and carries a message. Repair a failure with
`repository_retryProviderSetup`. Without a token, `providerSetup.status: ready` means that the
requested GitHub and Convex work finished. It does not mean Cloudflare is complete. This expected
pending state is not a failure and must not be repaired with the retry action. Cost: the created
resources run on the providers' free tiers; an idle app costs $0/month.

provisioning (optional, experimental) chooses who sets up the app. samebase is the default and
everything above describes it. With repository_actions, the repository's own GitHub Actions run
Alchemy, create the Convex project, and deploy the app to Convex. Samebase creates no provider
resource, and Cloudflare takes no part: the call needs only the GitHub and Convex connections, and
the result reports cloudflare.state none. Samebase creates the GitHub repository and writes two
values into it: the Actions secret CONVEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, which holds the credential of the
organization's Convex connection (its OAuth token or its API key), and the Actions variable
CONVEX_TEAM_ID. Then it seeds the GitHub Actions variant of the starter on main, and that first push
deploys. When GitHub created the repository with another default branch, Samebase makes main the
default before it pushes the starter, so that first deployment runs as production. The Convex
project takes the repository's name, so omit convexProjectName, cloudflareWorkerName,
buildTokenUuid, and convexDeploymentRegion. Before it creates anything, the call fails when the
organization has no Convex connection, when the Samebase GitHub App installation has not granted the
Secrets and Variables permissions, or when a Convex project with the repository's name exists. A
ready providerSetup then means that the secret and the variable are written and the starter is
seeded, not that the app is deployed: the deployment runs in the repository's GitHub Actions, and
`repository_getStatus` reports setupStack.state done after it finished. Samebase's Worker and Convex
project tools refuse such a repository, because its GitHub Actions own its provider resources.

## Arguments

- `githubOwnerLogin` (string, required): GitHub user or organization login that will own the new
  repository. Ask the user when it is unclear.
- `name` (string, required): Name for the new GitHub repository.
- `convexDeploymentRegion` (value, optional): Optional production region: aws-us-east-1,
  aws-eu-west-1, aws-ca-central-1, or aws-ap-southeast-2. Omit it to use the organization default,
  which is US East when no default is saved. Before you pass aws-eu-west-1, tell the user: EU usage
  costs 1.3 times US usage, and included usage for Starter and Professional plans does not apply to
  EU deployments (https://www.convex.dev/pricing).
- `buildTokenUuid` (string, optional): Optional Workers Builds token UUID. Omit it: Samebase uses
  the last-used token, else the only token, and lists the tokens when it needs the user's choice.
- `convexProjectName` (string, optional): Optional Convex project name. Defaults to the repository
  name.
- `cloudflareWorkerName` (string, optional): Optional Cloudflare Worker name. Defaults to the
  repository name.
- `description` (string, optional): Optional GitHub repository description.
- `private` (boolean, optional): Whether to create a private GitHub repository. Defaults to true.
- `provisioning` (value, optional): Optional, experimental. samebase (the default): Samebase creates
  the Convex project and the Worker. repository_actions: the repository's GitHub Actions run
  Alchemy, create the Convex project, and deploy the app to Convex, with no Cloudflare. Use it only
  when the user asks for it.

## Returns

JSON Schema for the tool's `structuredContent`:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "repositoryId": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "githubRepositoryFullName": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "cloudflare": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "state": {
              "const": "planned"
            },
            "workerName": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": ["state", "workerName"],
          "additionalProperties": false
        },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "state": {
              "const": "pending"
            },
            "setupGuideUrl": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": ["state", "setupGuideUrl"],
          "additionalProperties": false
        },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "state": {
              "const": "none"
            }
          },
          "required": ["state"],
          "additionalProperties": false
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": ["repositoryId", "githubRepositoryFullName", "cloudflare"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```
